name: Kustenaú
confidence_why: Kustenaú is known only from von den Steinen's 1894 wordlist, whose accent convention (penultimate unless marked, with a large share of words marked for final stress) is a transcription rule rather than a stress analysis, and the one later study, Corbera Mori & Ferreira 2022, works from that same list and restates the convention without analysing stress, so no source determines the stress system.

new_statements.quote: Em relação à representação do acento no Kustenau, Steinen menciona que, nos casos em que ele não é indicado, ocorre na penúltima sílaba da palavra.
new_statements.translation: Regarding the representation of the accent in Kustenau, Steinen mentions that, in cases where it is not indicated, it falls on the penultimate syllable of the word.

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Chapter 2 head on pdf p. 48 ('CAPÍTULO 2 / INTERPRETAÇÃO FONÉTICO-FONOLÓGICA DO KUSTENAU (ARAWAK)..', Corbera Mori & Ferreira), chapter ends printed p. 79 (Capítulo 3 begins pdf p. 80); pdf page = printed page (footers 'Capítulo 2 58', 'Capítulo 2 59'). The quoted sentence is there verbatim: last lines of p. 58 'Em relação à representação do' continuing on p. 59 'acento no Kustenau, Steinen menciona que, nos casos em que ele não é / indicado, ocorre na penúltima sílaba da palavra.' immediately before heading '4.1 Representação grafemática das vogais'. A a full-text search for stress/accent the whole chapter text (and of the full 330-page volume) for acento/acentu/tônic/stress/proemin/prosód…
new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Kustenaú has an empty rule and there are no existing statements, so this sentence adds the only placement information on record: penult as the unmarked default in von den Steinen's transcription, with many words marked for final stress. It is second-hand (relaying a 1894 orthographic convention), not a phonological analysis.
new_statements.rule_in_words: The chapter contains no stress analysis of its own; its single sentence on accent relays von den Steinen's (1894) transcription convention: where no accent mark is written, stress is on the penult; where the stress is elsewhere it is written with an acute accent. The wordlist data reproduced in the chapter (pp. 60-75) carry many marked non-penult forms, most of them word-final (nunéi 'tongue', itsá 'canoe', atú 'grandfather', mamá 'mother', uléi 'manioc', nutuló 'ear', nupatatá 'fingernail', kisuá 'white', uhú 'sweet potato', hemirzá 'red', zapalakú 'uluri', nuyuhiá 'eyelashes', numái 'skin', yakuí, nukitsíu..) and at least one marked antepenult (nutévoe 'tooth'), so 'penult' is only the unmarked default of the transcription, not a demonstrated fixed rule.
new_statements.exceptions: None discussed as such; but the data as transcribed show numerous acute-marked final-stress words and nutévoe with marked antepenult, i.e. the 1894 transcriber marked stress wherever it was not penult.
new_statements.identity_note: The chapter treats Kustenau as recorded by Karl von den Steinen in 1894 among the Xinguan Arawak peoples (Mehinaku, Kustenau, Waurá, Yaulapiti); Kustenau is extinct and the wordlist is its sole documentation. The comparative Mehinaku and Waurá data in the chapter (Corbera Mori's own fieldwork; Jackson & Richards 1966; Richards 2015) are other languages, not Kustenau, and were not used for the reading.

readall_conflicts: Only one work was listed and opened, so there is no disagreement between sources. Within the work there is an internal tension worth recording: the one explicit sentence gives penult as the default (unmarked) stress position of von den Steinen's 1894 transcription, while the Kustenau forms reproduced from that same wordlist carry acute-marked final stress in a large share of the vocabulary (nunéi, itsá, atú, mamá, uléi, nutuló, nupatatá, kisuá, uhú, hemirzá, zapalakú, nuyuhiá, numái, yakuí, nukitsíu, yutá, nuhuparáta..) and one marked antepenult (nutévoe). The chapter offers no phonological account of stress, no syllable-weight or morphological conditioning, and no statement on contrastiveness; the authors themselves note (p. 56) that Steinen's wordlist is the only material that exists for the language.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: Quote verified verbatim in held page images of pp. 529-530. Kustenaú is an extinct Xinguan Arawak lect whose entire documentation is von den Steinen's 1884/1887 wordlists; Glottolog has zero descriptive references beyond the 1894 wordlist. The only later study (Corbera Mori & Ferreira 2022, downloaded now from Editora UnB open access) works from the same list, restates the 'unmarked = penult' convention (pp. 58-59) and gives no stress analysis. No description states a stress rule, so not determinable from the transcription convention plus item-by-item marked deviations is the correct and final coding; nothing better can exist. Optional housekeeping only: add the 2022 chapter to the record's 'also checked' sources.
